To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of estradiol on endometrial cell proliferation may be mediated by IGF I secreted by endometrial stromal cells.
the effect of estrogen and insulin on human endometrial epithelium proliferation is enhanced by coculture with stromal cells and is mediated by stromal-secreted IGF-I.
the estrogenic and the insulin effects on EEC proliferation are mediated by ESC-derived soluble factors, in particular, IGF I.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new in vitro model for studying the role of endometrial stroma in the regulation of epithelial cell proliferation.

the identification of factors that can be used to improve the culture methods for human endometrial cells, which may lead to a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the endometrial response to hormones.
the identification of new mechanisms by which the endometrial epithelium may be stimulated by estrogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
estrogen and insulin effects on endometrial cells are mediated at least in large part by soluble factors secreted by ESC.
the effect of estradiol and insulin on human EEC is mediated through the production of IGF I by ESC.
17β- estradiol and insulin act synergistically in the regulation of EEC proliferation through ESC-secreted soluble factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stromal-epithelial interaction is an essential factor for estrogen responsiveness in endometrial epithelium.
17β- estradiol and insulin are able to stimulate EEC growth in the presence of ESC.
17β-estrogen and insulin effects are modulated by ESC-derived IGF I. Titolo: Stromal-Epithelium Interactions Modulate Estradiol Responsiveness in Normal Endometrium Autori: MELCHIORRI, Loredana
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coculture of EEC and ESC is a suitable model to study the mechanisms underlying estrogen action on EEC proliferation.
the use of the EEC/ESC in vitro model allows the identification of new mechanisms by which estrogens and insulin can modulate EEC growth.
the use of a coculture model allows us to demonstrate that estrogen and insulin can induce EEC proliferation.
